findings.evidence: "Passengers may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Replace with content specific to weekend service updates.
findings.violation: This paragraph is identical to s1-p1 in the "Accessibility improvements" section, creating confusing duplication between unrelated sections.

findings.fix: Either add aria-required="true" to the input and a non-color indicator like an asterisk, or remove the red styling.
findings.violation: The label is red but the input has no aria-required, aria-invalid, or asterisk to indicate why it's styled differently, violating WCAG color-only requirements.

findings.fix: Add meaningful alt text like alt="Delete" or, if decorative, add role="presentation".
findings.violation: The image has an empty alt attribute, making it inaccessible to screen readers even though it appears to be a functional delete button.

findings.evidence: Elements appear as `<div class="step" style="order:3">`, `<div class="step" style="order:2">`, `<div class="step" style="order:1">`
findings.fix: Reorder the HTML elements so step 1 appears first in the source, followed by step 2, then step 3.
findings.violation: The HTML source order (3, 2, 1) doesn't match the logical/visual order (1, 2, 3), breaking navigation for screen readers and users without CSS.

findings.evidence: Section titled "Schedule changes" contains `read the accessibility improvements list`
findings.fix: Update the link text to match its destination and context, such as "read the fare history" or change the URL to point to schedule changes.
findings.violation: The link text says "accessibility improvements" but it's in a "Schedule changes" section and points to "/fares/history", creating a contextual mismatch.

findings.fix: Set aria-invalid="false" initially or omit it, then set to "true" only after validation fails on user input.
findings.violation: The input has aria-invalid="true" on page load before any user interaction, creating a false error state that confuses users and screen readers.
